Header: Bean Common Mosaic Virus (BCMV) Ububembe bw’ibishyimbo in Kinyarwanda

Prevention: Use healthy/certified seeds (available from seed multipliers, agrodealers, RAB)
Muhondo (G2331), Nyiramata (CAB2), RWR2154, RWV3316, MAC44, RWV1129, RWR2245)
Use fertilizers to help plants be more vigorous, basal application of organic fertilizer 20-30ton/Ha and
Clean field tools (eg clean hoe by heat, etc.) after use
Avoid movement in the field /touching from infected to non-infected plants
Control aphids in the field and other fields around (see direct control)
Monitoring: Monitor the field from 2 weeks after planting to flowering
Observe the leaves for symptoms which include: mosaic, necrosis, downward curling on leaves; stunting, irregular shape leaves, light- yellow and dark green areas in a mosaic pattern.
Monitor the disease symptoms especially during flowering early morning
Take action if you find 1 plant infected
Monitor for the presence of aphids on shoots, stem and leaves
Threshold for aphids is 20 aphids on 2.5 cm of shoot
Direct Control: Uproot infected plants and burry as soon as spotted
Soapy water on plants and under leaves; (mix 8 gr of soap in 10 liters of water and spray on plants); Mix 1 kg of
Neem leaves with 5 liters of water and boil them till the colour of leaves become yellow.
After 12 hours you mix the extracted juice with water and spray on plants.
You need 80kg of leaves for 1 ha
Restrictions: Do not eat or drink while manipulating pesticide
EC, (20ml/20L of water at 14 days interval)
II (Moderately hazardous); contact insecticide; Do not harvest before 6 days after the last application.
Avoid spraying when plants in flower or near water sources.
II (Moderately hazardous); Contact insecticide; Do not harvest before 14 days after the last application; It is toxic to bees and aquatic organisms.
